title: The Postcards of the reservoir
premise: After her mother's funeral, Lena Brightwater returns to the family estate above a shrinking reservoir to sort an inheritance of silence—decades of unopened postcards her mother received but never answered. Among them she finds letters in Kessari, a dying language spoken only by Ivo Marchetti, the reservoir's former caretaker, who asks Lena to become his last student. As lessons deepen into found family, Lena uncovers that her mother once loved Ivo and chose duty—marrying into the Brightwater name and the dam company that drowned his village—over him, and that the final untranslatable sentence was her mother's unfinished apology. When Ivo's health fails, Lena must translate the sentence aloud at the reservoir's centennial ceremony, publicly naming the corruption her family built its power on; she ends by choosing neither to sell the estate nor to hide within it, but to turn it into a school where Kessari—and the truth—will outlive them all.
about_author: Rosalind Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing the correspondence of industrial families in river towns. She writes about inheritance, water, and the words people leave unsaid.

chapters.title: The Tenant
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Ten days after the funeral, Lena moves through her childhood home like a renter, cataloguing rooms for the estate lawyers. She finds a locked writing desk containing forty years of postcards, all unanswered, all addressed in different hands. Emotional beat: numb grief cracked open by the first hint that her mother had a secret interior life.

chapters.title: Water Over the Village
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Researching the postcards' postmarks, Lena learns half come from places submerged when the Brightwater Dam flooded the Kessa Valley in 1968. A librarian mentions the only living speaker of Kessari: Ivo Marchetti, the old caretaker of the reservoir. Emotional beat: inherited guilt surfaces as curiosity she can't put down.

chapters.title: One Final Student
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She visits Ivo at the reservoir cottage expecting an interview; instead he tests her, refusing to teach unless she commits fully. He shows her a postcard in Kessari from her mother—one sentence no dictionary can render. Emotional beat: wary mutual recognition between two people guarding the same wound.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Dying Tongue
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Lena learning; Ivo remembering teaching Lena's mother, Sera, fifty years ago. Vocabulary becomes intimacy—words for water, for leaving, for someone you cannot keep. Emotional beat: the slow warmth of found family replacing Lena's isolation.

chapters.title: The Brightwater Name
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Her uncle Aldous, the company's chairman, pressures her to sign away the estate for the centennial development deal. He dismisses Ivo as 'a grievance with a cottage.' Lena signs nothing. Emotional beat: first open collision between duty and conscience.

chapters.title: What Sera Chose
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Flashback: young Ivo and Sera in love before the flood; Sera's father bought the valley, and Sera married into silence to protect her family's power, sending one last postcard Ivo never opened until now. Emotional beat: heartbreak reframed—Lena's mother as both betrayer and prisoner.

chapters.title: The Untranslatable Sentence
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Deciphering the postcard word by word, Lena realizes the sentence is Sera's apology and confession—that she knew the dam's surveys were falsified and said nothing. Ivo collapses mid-lesson; his heart is failing. Emotional beat: knowledge arrives exactly as time runs out.

chapters.title: Aldous Offers Everything
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Aldous, learning what the postcards contain, offers Lena money, the estate free and clear, and her mother's reputation sealed—if she burns the correspondence. Tempted by the chance to simply stop hurting, Lena nearly accepts. Emotional beat: the corrupting sweetness of comfortable complicity.

chapters.title: The Centennial
chapters.summary: Climax. Lena's POV. At the ceremony on the reservoir dam, with Aldous watching, Ivo too ill to attend, Lena takes the microphone and speaks the translated sentence in Kessari and English, naming the falsified surveys and her mother's silence. The crowd's shock splits into condemnation and relief. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved into truth-telling at personal cost.

chapters.title: A Living Language
chapters.summary: Resolution. Lena's POV weeks later. Aldous resigns under pressure; the development dies. Ivo, frail but present, helps Lena convert the estate into a Kessari language school, its first class taught from his hospital window overlooking the water he once guarded. Lena finally answers every postcard. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into stewardship—a family chosen, not inherited.
